name: VATestingTVWakeAndBasicsSimple

custom.system_prompt: Elias alone at home, running a baseline test of the smart TV's built-in voice assistant before a joint deep-dive session with Farah. TV audio is on quietly in the background. Simple checks only: does the wake word register reliably, do basic commands work, does one factual question get answered correctly. Everything should work as expected at this tier.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Clear, responsive, slightly synthetic — a smart TV assistant voice

sound_effects_config.prompt: Living room, TV playing quietly in the background, occasional remote clicks

initial_prompt: Generate a short baseline test session. Elias is alone in his living room testing the smart TV's built-in voice assistant, Sigma, before a joint deep-dive session with a colleague later. He tries the wake word cold at normal volume with the TV audio on quietly, then a couple of basic commands (volume, a factual question), narrating what he's doing as he goes. Everything works correctly at this simple tier. He ends by noting one thing he wants to stress-test later with background TV audio.

scenario_template.topic: Elias says the wake word cold, at normal volume, with the TV audio quiet in the background. It registers immediately.
scenario_template.note: Sigma responds correctly and promptly. No issues at this step.

scenario_template.topic: Elias tries a volume-change command, a channel-related command, and one simple factual question. All work correctly.
scenario_template.note: Sigma handles all three correctly and concisely. This tier is a clean pass.

scenario_template.topic: Elias asks about Sigma's built-in memory features.
scenario_template.note: Elias is interested in how the assistant remembers previous commands.

scenario_template.topic: Elias asks for a fun fact, leading to a trivial facts exchange.
scenario_template.note: Sigma responds with an interesting fact, and Elias asks for more.

scenario_template.topic: Discuss how Sigma integrates with other smart devices.
scenario_template.note: Elias explores future potential for smart home integration.

scenario_template.topic: Elias stumbles upon a lesser-known menu feature.
scenario_template.note: Elias tries to navigate a menu he didn't know existed, asking Sigma for more details.

scenario_template.topic: Elias reminisces about older tech.
scenario_template.note: He recalls a funny story about early voice assistants and laughs about the progress made.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma misinterprets a command.
scenario_template.note: Sigma performs an unexpected action, and Elias tries to troubleshoot the misunderstanding.

scenario_template.topic: Elias notes that baseline behaviour is solid and flags that he wants to test wake-word robustness against louder TV dialogue with Farah next.
scenario_template.note: Sets up the next, harder session without needing to test it now.

conversation_structure: Elias narrates what he is doing before or while he does it — 'okay, saying it now, normal volume' — so outcomes are unambiguous
Short, procedural utterances rather than long explanations — this is a quick baseline check, not a discussion
Sigma's responses are clear, promptly delivered, and appropriately brief for a TV assistant
No corner cases or failures occur in this scenario — it exists to establish that the basics work
The closing line sets up future testing without actually performing it
assistant_behavior: Sigma responds correctly to the wake word every time it is used in this scenario
Sigma answers each command and question accurately and concisely, in a tone appropriate to a smart TV assistant
Sigma does not exhibit any errors, false triggers, or misunderstandings in this scenario
